past_medical_history: Right middle cerebral artery infarct 10 weeks ago, treated with intravenous thrombolysis, NIHSS 12 at presentation and 3 at discharge

social_history.living_situation: Lives with his wife; a daughter visits at weekends
social_history.driving: Not driving since the stroke; formal assessment pending

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person and place, year correct, month incorrect. MoCA 20/30 with losses in trail-making, cube, clock, digit span backwards, serial sevens and delayed recall (3/5 unaided, 5/5 cued). Mild left-sided inattention on cancellation (3 omissions). Insight into the deficits is partial.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full, mild gaze preference to the right on distraction. Left homonymous inattention without a field cut on formal confrontation. Left nasolabial flattening.
neurological_exam.motor: Left arm 4+/5 proximally and 4/5 distally, left leg 5-/5. Tone increased in the left arm. Left pronator drift.
neurological_exam.sensory: Reduced light touch and graphaesthesia on the left; extinction on double simultaneous stimulation.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 3+ on the left, 2+ on the right, left plantar extensor.
neurological_exam.coordination: Limited on the left by weakness.
neurological_exam.gait: Hemiparetic with circumduction of the left leg, using a stick. No falls since discharge.
neurological_exam.additional: Pulse regular at 78. No carotid bruit. No tremor. Mood reactive, denies persistent low mood.

patient.chief_complaint: Ten weeks after a stroke he cannot manage at home cognitively, beyond what his weakness explains
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Pietro Lombardi is a 75-year-old retired site manager who had a right middle cerebral artery infarct ten weeks ago, thrombolysed with a fall in NIHSS from 12 to 3. His motor recovery has been good: he walks with a stick and uses the left hand for gross tasks. His wife's concern is different. Since discharge he has not been able to resume anything requiring organisation: he cannot follow the sequence of his own medication, has twice set out for the pharmacy and returned without going in, and cannot manage the household bills he handled until the day of the stroke. He loses the thread of a conversation with two other people present, misses objects on his left in the kitchen, and does not seem fully aware of the extent of his difficulties. He remembers events when reminded of the context. There has been slow improvement in the motor deficit over ten weeks with no corresponding improvement in the organisational difficulty. He denies low mood, sleeps adequately and engages with rehabilitation willingly. There are no hallucinations, no fluctuation in alertness and no dream enactment. His blood pressure at discharge and since has been in the 145-155 range and his HbA1c is 7.9%.

findings.location: Right frontoparietal cortex and subcortical white matter, right middle cerebral artery superior division

signal_characteristics.T2_FLAIR: Cortical and subcortical gliosis with early encephalomalacia and ex vacuo dilatation of the adjacent lateral ventricle
signal_characteristics.SWI: Petechial haemorrhagic transformation within the infarct, chronic, without mass effect

findings.type: White matter hyperintensity of presumed vascular origin

findings.location: Focal about the infarct; medial temporal lobes preserved

signal_characteristics.Coronal_T1: Hippocampi symmetric and normal for age

volumetrics.infarct_volume: Approximately 34 mL, right middle cerebral artery superior division

additional_observations: The infarct involves the right frontoparietal cortex including the attentional network, matching the residual left-sided inattention and the dysexecutive profile
Petechial haemorrhagic transformation within the infarct is chronic and expected after thrombolysis; it is not a new haemorrhage
The pre-existing small-vessel burden of Fazekas 2 with one lacune was present before the stroke and lowers the cognitive reserve
Medial temporal lobes are preserved, so there is no imaging evidence of a coexisting Alzheimer atrophy pattern
mri.impression: Established right middle cerebral artery superior division infarct of approximately 34 mL with chronic petechial haemorrhagic transformation, on a background of Fazekas 2 small-vessel disease and one lacune. The lesion accounts for the attentional, executive and visuospatial profile; medial temporal lobes are preserved.

findings: Voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy
No atrial fibrillation; inpatient telemetry during the stroke admission showed sinus rhythm for 72 hours
ecg.interpretation: Sinus rhythm with left ventricular hypertrophy. No atrial fibrillation here or on 72 hours of inpatient telemetry, consistent with the large-artery mechanism established during the acute admission.

labs.interpretation: HbA1c 7.9% is above target for secondary prevention. LDL 78 mg/dL on rosuvastatin remains above the post-stroke target of 70 mg/dL. TSH, B12, folate, RPR and HIV are normal or negative, so no reversible cause is contributing to the post-stroke cognitive impairment.

findings.signal: Irregular plaque with 50-60% stenosis by NASCET criteria; peak systolic velocity 182 cm/s, unchanged from the acute study
findings.description: Moderate stenosis, ipsilateral to the infarct

advanced_imaging.impression: Moderate right internal carotid stenosis, ipsilateral to the infarct and stable since the acute admission. Below the 70% threshold at which revascularisation is offered; management remains intensive medical therapy.

specialized_test.impression: Attentional, executive and visuoconstructional impairment with residual left-sided inattention, preserved naming and recognition memory, and informant-rated loss of instrumental independence. The pattern maps onto the right middle cerebral artery infarct, and the functional impairment places it at the dementia rather than the mild impairment threshold.

findings.performance: Digit span backwards 0/1, serial sevens 2/3, left-sided inattention — impaired
Trail-making 0/1, clock 1/3, sequencing failures at home — impaired

clinical_assessment.impression: MoCA 20/30 ten weeks after a right middle cerebral artery infarct, with executive, attentional and visuospatial impairment, residual left-sided inattention and cue-responsive recall. The cognitive deficit exceeds what the motor deficit explains and has not tracked the motor recovery. The Geriatric Depression Scale of 4/15 does not account for it.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.query: vascular cognitive impairment diagnostic criteria and secondary prevention

results.title: Diagnostic criteria for vascular cognitive disorders: a VASCOG statement
results.authors: Sachdev P, Kalaria R, O'Brien J, et al.
results.summary: Requires a cognitive syndrome documented on a validated instrument plus imaging or temporal evidence that cerebrovascular disease accounts for it.

results.title: Neuroimaging standards for research into small vessel disease (STRIVE-2)
results.authors: Duering M, Biessels GJ, Brodtmann A, et al.
results.summary: Defines and standardises the reporting of white matter hyperintensity, lacunes, microbleeds, perivascular spaces and cortical superficial siderosis.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for vascular cognitive impairment; management is control of the vascular risk factors, secondary prevention matched to the mechanism, review of the anticholinergic burden, and treatment of coexisting Alzheimer pathology where biomarkers support it.

medication_review.proposed: review of the current medication list for anticholinergic burden
warnings: Anticholinergic load is a reversible contributor to cognitive impairment in this population and should be quantified before any new prescription.
medication_review.summary: No prohibitive interaction identified within the current list.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Post-stroke vascular dementia following a right middle cerebral artery superior division infarct, on a background of pre-existing moderate small-vessel disease

differential.key_features: Common at ten weeks and a genuine confounder, but he denies low mood, the Geriatric Depression Scale is 4/15, he engages with rehabilitation, and the deficit is attentional and executive with objective left-sided inattention
Alertness is stable with no fluctuation, no new medication and no infective or metabolic trigger

differential.diagnosis: Alzheimer's disease unmasked by the stroke
differential.key_features: There is no premorbid history of cognitive decline, the hippocampi are preserved, and recall is cue-responsive; a biomarker would be required to raise this and nothing in the presentation calls for it

differential.diagnosis: Expected early post-stroke cognitive recovery trajectory
differential.key_features: Cognitive deficits at ten weeks may still improve, which is why the diagnosis is dated from the event and reassessed — but the functional impairment now is real and requires management now
No fluctuation, hallucinations, spontaneous parkinsonism or dream enactment

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a collateral history from an informant who sees the patient daily: the shape of the decline (abrupt, stepwise or gradual), whether any step can be dated to a cerebrovascular event, and which instrumental activities have been lost
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Cognitive impairment beginning with a documented stroke ten weeks ago, disproportionate to the residual motor deficit, non-progressive and not explained by mood, with loss of previously held instrumental competence

optimal_actions.action: Perform a validated bedside cognitive assessment and record the per-domain profile and whether delayed recall improves with cueing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: MoCA 20/30 with executive, attentional and visuospatial impairment and residual left-sided inattention, disproportionate to the residual motor deficit and not attributable to mood

optimal_actions.action: Order the reversible-cause screen and the vascular-risk assays that will be treated (CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, RPR, HIV, HbA1c, lipid panel)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Reversible contributors excluded; HbA1c 7.9% and LDL 78 mg/dL both above post-stroke targets

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI reported in STRIVE-2 terms — FLAIR for white matter hyperintensity with a Fazekas grade, T1/T2 for lacunes, DWI to establish that the lesions are chronic, and SWI for microbleeds and cortical superficial siderosis — together with the medial temporal atrophy grade
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Established right frontoparietal infarct of about 34 mL with chronic petechial haemorrhagic transformation, on a Fazekas 2 background, with preserved medial temporal lobes

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to look for atrial fibrillation as the embolic source and for the left ventricular hypertrophy of chronic hypertension
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sinus rhythm with left ventricular hypertrophy and no atrial fibrillation, consistent with the mechanism already established acutely

optimal_actions.action: Image the extracranial carotid arteries to establish whether a large-artery source accounts for the cortical infarcts
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Right internal carotid stenosis of 50-60%, unchanged from the acute admission and below the threshold for revascularisation, confirming the large-artery mechanism already established

optimal_actions.action: Order formal multi-domain neuropsychological testing to settle the executive-versus-amnestic attribution and to document a baseline for follow-up
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Right-hemisphere-weighted attentional and executive profile with preserved recognition — post-stroke cognitive impairment reaching the dementia threshold on functional grounds

optimal_actions.action: Confirm the diagnostic criteria applied and the current secondary-prevention targets against the guidelines
optimal_actions.expected_finding: VASCOG 2014 criteria and the 2021 AHA/ASA secondary prevention targets confirmed

optimal_actions.action: Review the medication list for anticholinergic burden and for the interaction between antithrombotic choice and the microbleed burden before prescribing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Anticholinergic contributors identified and the antithrombotic choice reconciled with the imaging burden

optimal_actions.action: Continue and intensify secondary prevention — blood pressure toward a systolic below 130 mmHg, HbA1c below 7.5%, LDL below 70 mg/dL, single antiplatelet therapy — refer for cognitive rehabilitation targeting attention and executive function alongside the physical rehabilitation, complete the formal driving assessment, and plan cognitive reassessment at six and twelve months since post-stroke deficits can still evolve
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Secondary prevention intensified, cognitive rehabilitation added to the physical programme, driving formally assessed, and a reassessment timeline set because the post-stroke trajectory is not yet fixed

optimal_actions.action: Disclose the diagnosis and its mechanism to the patient and the informant, and address driving, medication management, finances, advance care planning and caregiver support
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Patient and informant engaged in care planning; safety domains addressed

useless_tools.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome
The MRI already obtained answers everything a CT could and more: CT cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so it cannot grade the vascular burden this diagnosis rests on
There is no embolic lesion pattern to explain: the burden here is small-vessel, and a structural cardioembolic source would not account for it
Prolonged rhythm monitoring is for an unexplained embolic infarct pattern; in pure small-vessel disease it changes nothing about the diagnosis or the treatment

sequence_constraints.reason: Document the cognitive deficit before attributing it: imaging read without a cognitive profile invites over-attribution of incidental white matter change

critical_actions: Screen cognition after stroke rather than assuming that motor recovery represents recovery
Establish the temporal relationship: onset within three months of a documented stroke satisfies the NINDS-AIREN criterion
Distinguish post-stroke cognitive impairment from post-stroke depression with formal scales
Document the deficit and its functional consequence with an informant-rated scale to place it at the dementia threshold
Obtain MRI and relate the cognitive profile to the infarct territory and the pre-existing small-vessel burden
Intensify secondary prevention, since recurrent stroke is the main determinant of further decline
Refer for cognitive rehabilitation and complete the driving assessment; plan reassessment because the trajectory can still change
contraindicated_actions: Do not attribute post-stroke cognitive impairment to depression without formal assessment
Do not read the chronic petechial haemorrhagic transformation as a new haemorrhage and stop the antiplatelet
Do not defer secondary prevention until cognition is 'settled' — recurrent stroke is the main risk to cognition
Do not certify fitness to drive on the strength of motor recovery when attentional neglect is documented
Do not prescribe anticholinergic or sedating medications during cognitive rehabilitation
key_reasoning_points: Post-stroke dementia is diagnosed on the temporal criterion: cognitive decline beginning within three months of a documented stroke, with a deficit that the lesion can explain
Motor and cognitive recovery dissociate after stroke, and a good NIHSS improvement says nothing about executive function
Pre-existing small-vessel disease lowers cognitive reserve and helps explain why a single infarct produced a dementia in this patient
Chronic petechial haemorrhagic transformation after thrombolysis is expected and is not a reason to withdraw antiplatelet therapy
Cognitive deficits at ten weeks can still evolve, so the diagnosis carries a reassessment plan rather than being treated as fixed

red_herrings.intended_effect: Read as a new intracerebral haemorrhage, prompting withdrawal of antiplatelet therapy
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Petechial haemorrhagic transformation within a thrombolysed infarct is chronic and expected; it does not contraindicate secondary-prevention antiplatelet therapy

red_herrings.data_point: Good motor recovery from NIHSS 12 to 3
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests the stroke has largely resolved and that the cognitive complaints must be functional or depressive
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Motor and cognitive recovery dissociate; the attentional and executive deficits with objective left-sided omissions map onto the frontoparietal infarct and have not tracked the motor improvement

key_educational_points: Cognitive screening belongs in every post-stroke review; motor recovery does not predict cognitive recovery
The three-month temporal criterion is what defines post-stroke dementia
Pre-existing small-vessel burden lowers reserve and helps explain why one infarct caused a dementia
Petechial haemorrhagic transformation after thrombolysis is expected and does not contraindicate antiplatelet therapy
